Democracy Defender Mod Manager (DDMM), release candidate 15: *your mods, your democracy, defended.* It's still an
early build, but it's meant to be usable by anyone, not just developers.

**The DDMM Promise, in brief:** every mod is welcome (DDMM never blocks, blacklists or ranks mods or mod sites),
no account is ever needed on any site, your files stay in a folder you control, it's Apache-2.0 open source
forever, and update checks never run unless you ask.

## Quick start

1. **Download** the right file for you (see the table below).
2. **Run it.** DDMM looks for your Helldivers 2 install automatically. If Steam is in its usual place, there's
   nothing to set up.
3. **Add mods and click Deploy.** Drag in an archive or folder, or click "Add URL" and paste a link.

**Works with AyakaMods, Nexus Mods, ModWorkshop, GameBanana, GitHub, any direct link, or files already on your
disk.** Special love to the AyakaMods community ❤️, one of the best homes for Helldivers 2 modding. Go say hi:
<https://ayakamods.com/games/helldivers-2.119/>.

## Which file do I download?

| You want... | Download |
| --- | --- |
| A normal install on Windows (Start Menu shortcut, uninstaller) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.15-windows-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows without installing anything (unzip and run) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.15-windows-x64-portable.zip` |
| Linux: Fedora, Nobara, openSUSE (`dnf`/`zypper`) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.15-linux-x86_64.rpm` |
| Linux: Debian, Ubuntu, Mint (`apt`) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.15-linux-amd64.deb` |
| Linux: other distros, no install (uses your desktop's graphics libraries) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.15-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux: Arch/CachyOS, or just the binary (needs WebKitGTK 4.1) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.15-linux-x64.tar.gz` |

Linux install commands, the dependencies for each distro, and fixes for a blank window or AppImage/FUSE errors
are in [Installing on Linux](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/getting-started/linux/).

**One-click install (optional):** also grab the browser extension: `ddmm-extension-chrome-1.0.1.zip`
(Chrome, Edge, Brave) or `ddmm-extension-firefox-1.0.1.zip` (Firefox). See
[One-click install](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/using/one-click-install/).

Check `SHA256SUMS.txt` if you want to verify your download.

## What's new in 2.0.0-rc.15

No new bug reports came in after rc.14, so this round went looking for bugs instead. Here's what turned up.

### Deploy and Purge

- **One broken mod no longer removes all your mods from the game.** If a mod's manifest named an option folder that
  wasn't in the mod, Deploy used to clear the game's mod files first and only then stop with an error, leaving the
  game with no mods at all. Deploy now checks every mod first, and leaves the previous deploy in place if anything
  is wrong.
- **Purge no longer deletes game files the Skip List protects.** This also affected every Deploy, since Deploy
  purges first. DDMM now keeps a small list of the files it deployed (`.ddmm-deployed.json` in the game's `data`
  folder), and only removes a skip-listed game file if DDMM put it there and it hasn't changed since.
  **If you used the Skip List with rc.14 or earlier, verify the game files in Steam once** (Library → Helldivers 2
  → Properties → Installed Files → Verify integrity of game files). Older versions could delete the game's own
  files for those names.
- **Deploy keeps your option fixes.** When a mod's options changed (for example after an update) and Deploy reset
  them to the defaults, Deploy used the reset options, but the next save wrote the old ones back. Fixed.

### Installing mods

- **Mods zipped as a folder now install with all their options.** If a mod's archive had everything inside one
  folder (`Mod Name/manifest.json`), DDMM ignored the author's manifest, so you lost the mod's options, pictures and
  descriptions, and adding it again made a duplicate. DDMM now finds the manifest inside the folder. Mods you
  already installed this way switch to the author's manifest on their next update, and their profile entries move
  with them (on, off and order are kept; the mod's options start from the author's defaults).
- **Big downloads no longer fail after 10 minutes.** Add from URL and mod updates gave up on any download still
  running at 10 minutes. Now a download only fails if it stalls for a minute or slows to a crawl (less than 1 MiB
  in 5 minutes).

### Mods page and Settings

- **Deleting a mod deletes the right one.** If a mod arrived from the browser or an import while "Are you sure?"
  was open, the wrong mod could be deleted. Fixed.
- **Keys no longer reach the page behind a popup.** Pressing Enter or Space while a popup was open could press the
  page's button again (for example, deploying three times).
- **Settings are saved when you close DDMM from the Settings page,** and if a save fails you're told why instead
  of losing your changes silently. A broken `settings.json` no longer traps you on the Settings page.
- The browser download popup no longer restarts or gets stuck on "Waiting..." when another popup covers it, and a
  file you pick by hand with "I already downloaded it" now shows up in the Mods list right away instead of after a
  restart.
- Settings can no longer be read half-written, and clicking "Always allow" in the browser extension while Settings
  is open no longer gets undone by saving Settings.

### Browser extension (one-click install)

The browser extension is now **1.0.1** (`ddmm-extension-chrome-1.0.1.zip`, `ddmm-extension-firefox-1.0.1.zip`).
If you use one-click install, update it the same way you installed it.

- With auto-capture on, installing one mod no longer marks every open tab of that site as "Installed ✓". And
  installing a different mod from a link you right-clicked no longer reports its result on the page's own button.
- On sites where the button starts the download itself (GitHub, GameBanana, ModWorkshop, and AyakaMods when you're
  logged in), it no longer gets stuck on "Installing…" when the download is cancelled or fails; you get a clear
  message and can try again.
- **Firefox:** if DDMM isn't installed, the extension now offers "Get DDMM" instead of saying DDMM will start.
- On Linux, the file DDMM uses to talk to the extension is private to your account from the moment it's created.

Thanks to everyone testing the release candidates. o7

**Skipped a few?** rc.10 had important safety fixes, rc.11 fixed mod deletion, rc.12 fixed mod option dropdowns, rc.13 fixed AyakaMods update checks and rc.14 fixed the Mods page stuck on "Loading..."; see the [releases page](https://github.com/katsyk/DemocracyDefenderModManager/releases).

## Known limitations

- **Windows builds are unsigned.** Windows SmartScreen will likely show a warning the first time you run the
  installer or the app. Click **"More info" → "Run anyway"** to continue.
- **The Linux .rpm and .deb are unsigned**, so openSUSE needs `zypper install --allow-unsigned-rpm`.
- **This is still a release candidate.** Expect some rough edges, and please report what you find.
